## Critical TSLA caveat

TSLA's addition in December 2020 is by far the largest S&P 500 inclusion in modern
history: the stock rose **+59.2%** between announcement (2020-11-16) and effective
date (2020-12-21) — a 25-business-day window driven by record index-fund buying of
~$80 billion.  This outlier single-handedly inflates the mean pop.

**Ex-TSLA mean pop: +0.02% (HAC t = +0.03).** The signal is entirely one event.

## Pop window results (announce → effective date)

| Metric | Full sample (n=46) | Ex-TSLA (n=45) |
|---|--:|--:|
| Mean return | **+1.31%** | **+0.02%** |
| Median return | +0.03% | 0.00% |
| Std dev | 10.18% | 5.29% |
| Win-rate | 50.0% | 48.9% |
| HAC *t* | **+0.86** | **+0.03** |

No horizon clears the inference bar (|*t*| ≥ 2) in either sample.
The full-sample t = 0.86 is purely TSLA-driven — a single event, not a repeatable signal.

## Give-back window results (post-effective date)

| Window | n | Mean return | Median | Win-rate | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1m (~21d after effective) | 46 | **+0.73%** | +1.16% | 52.2% | **+0.37** |
| 3m (~63d after effective) | 46 | **+10.92%** | +6.75% | 69.6% | **+2.84** |

**There is no give-back.** Post-inclusion returns are flat at 1m and
significantly *positive* at 3m — new S&P 500 members continue to outperform in
the months after joining, the opposite of the reversal narrative. The 3m t = +2.84
clears the bar but in the wrong direction for the give-back trade.

## Could you trade the pop?

The announced-to-effective pop strategy requires:
- Buying at announcement-day close (no look-ahead).
- Selling at effective-date close.
- A round-trip transaction cost of 10 bps is conservative for institutional desks.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Gross mean pop (all) | +1.31% |
| Net after 10 bps RT | +1.21% |
| Ex-TSLA gross | +0.02% |
| Ex-TSLA net after 10 bps | −0.08% |
| Implied annualised (avg 8-day window) | n/a — not a calendar strategy |

Without TSLA the pop is essentially zero gross. Execution reality is worse: the stock
price already moves on announcement day (before the close you can buy at), reducing
the achievable pop further.

Note: the 2020–2024 period includes TSLA (59.2% pop). Without it the 2020–2024 mean
drops to near zero. No period clears |*t*| ≥ 2.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Weak.** The gross mean pop is +1.31% (HAC *t* = +0.86), driven entirely
  by the TSLA outlier. Ex-TSLA the signal is +0.02% (*t* = +0.03) — statistically
  indistinguishable from noise. Literature support is strong (the classic 1986–2002
  effect is well-documented), but current-sample evidence is Weak at best.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** No significant gross edge in the post-2001 sample;
  ex-TSLA the trade is essentially flat gross. Transaction costs (bid-ask slippage
  on announcement day, market impact for large inclusion) consume the residual.
  ~2–3 index addition events per year in a liquid universe — too thin for a portfolio.
- **Give-back trade? — Absent/Wrong direction.** Post-inclusion 3m returns are
  significantly *positive* (+10.9%, *t* = +2.84), the opposite of a reversal. The
  "sell when it enters the index" trade does not work in this sample.
